newsitem.title: INDIA: BPL says withdraws ADR on negative India sentiment.
newsitem.headline: BPL says withdraws ADR on negative India sentiment.

text.p: Fledgling Indian telcommunications firm BPL Cellular Holdings said on Thursday it withdrew its issue of American Depositary Receipts (ADR) due to the current negative sentiment for Indian stocks.

"... given the prevailing negative sentiments towards Indian stocks it is quite likely that the stock would have been priced at a substantial discount to its true value and in addition, with a likelihood of performing poorly in the aftermarket," the firm said in a statement.
The $200 million ADR issue was to be India's first.
BPL said it was working on an alternate plan to meet its funding requirements.

"Morgan Stanley is working with the company on an alternate financing plan to meet its immediate requirements as it goes about rolling out its telecom services projects," the statement said. Morgan Stanley was global coordinator to the issue.

"The company believes that it will come back to the international market with an IPO. The company continues to believe that the international markets are the best sources of finance for telecom and other infrastructure projects," BPL said in the statement.
Investment bankers said investors were unwilling to pay the indicative price of $15-$17 for the issue.

"We had a good response as far as the book was concerned but we are not sure whether they were long-term investors. And we were not sure that the price we were getting was representative of the real price of the stock," one source close to the deal said.
He said investors were willing to pay from $10 upwards.
